title: Effects closer to the originals, more of FL Studio, Session mixer and Drum Rack, a first-song tour
summary: LYNX SHARE's reverbs, delays, modulation effects, dynamics and voice tools were refitted against the plugins they are modelled on, and projects saved earlier keep their sound. More of FL Studio's windows and menus are in, the Clip-launch workflow gains a Session mixer, a Drum Rack and map modes, many of Live's own devices now open from .als sets, FL Studio Mobile projects gain DW Sampler and Slicer, and the Simple workflow gets an Effects tab and a first-song tour. LYNX SHARE also has a new logo, by w3teal.
new: **Effects closer to the originals**: Epoch Verb, Atrium, Foil Plate, Halo, Horizon and Nebula, Orbit, Spiral Echo, Lattice Mod, Gemini Doubler and Echoform have a measured law, and Sentry, Hush, Glow, Voice Shift and Quell gained controls measured on the plugins they are modelled on. Orbit's tail score went from 6.32 to 8.27 and Nebula's from 5.84 to 8.43 (out of 10). New instances use the measured law; projects and presets saved earlier load the classic one and sound exactly as before.

**Remote control settings**, as in FL Studio: right-click a control › Link to controller... opens the window with the port, channel, controller, the mapping formula, smoothing and FL's Mode list, for knobs, notes and buttons. Automation clips have FL's 13 curve modes per point, and the Piano roll gains Limit, Scale levels, Flip and Randomize tools.

**Edison** on a mixer slot, as in FL Studio: it records now, on input or on play, keeps recording with its window closed and comes in from FL projects with its audio. Tools › One-click audio recording records into Edison or the Playlist.

**The Sampler page in FL Studio's layout**: Content, Playback with loop points, ping pong and start offset, Time stretching, Precomputed effects with crossfade and trim, and the waveform. LYNX SHARE's own controls are in a last box. (#156)

**Session mixer and Drum Rack** (Clip-launch workflow): under the clip grid each track has its input, sends, track delay and volume, as in Live. A Drum Rack has 16 pads, choke groups and return chains; Live sets bring theirs in as one Drum Rack, and .als export writes it.

**Scenes, Draw Mode and map modes** (Clip-launch workflow): duplicate, capture and insert scenes, give a scene its own tempo and time signature, record into clip slots, draw automation in steps (B), and link MIDI controls or computer keys to clips, scenes and knobs with MIDI and Key Map Modes (Ctrl+M / Ctrl+K). Browser colour collections and hot-swap (Q) are there too.

**Live's own devices** open from .als sets as LYNX SHARE's own, with their settings and automation: EQ Eight, EQ Three, Compressor, Glue Compressor, Multiband Dynamics, Limiter, Gate, Utility, Reverb, Delay, Echo, Auto Filter, Saturator, Drum Buss and more, plus Simpler, Drift and Operator without FM. Several were fitted to Live's own renders.

**FL Studio Mobile (.flm)**: DW Sampler and Slicer play on FL Studio Mobile's own engines, nine more effects come in on its own engines, instrument, pitch bend and controller lanes become automation, and chord sets and the key locker become the project's chords and key.

**Simple workflow**: a track dock with an Effects tab (eight one-knob effects, 22 chain presets and a Blend knob), an Instrument tab, a Keyboard tab with Scale keys and a Chord pad, and an Editor tab with the Piano roll. Loops follow the project key. A Welcome screen offers a seven-step first-song tour and two new demo songs, Late Bus and Sunrise.

**Lyrics and notes, Reference match and Clean voice** (in every layout): write lyrics beside the Playlist, match the Master's tone and loudness to a reference track, and put a ready voice chain on a track.
better: **Apex Limiter**: with True peak on, the output now stays under the ceiling at every oversampling setting (it could go up to 2.85 dB over), and the true-peak meters read within 0.03 dB. The Finish dock's Master looks now stay under −1 dBTP.
**Playback as in FL Studio**: a later clip of the same pattern takes over from an earlier one (#158), and when two notes of the same key overlap, each note's end stops only its own voice.

**FL Studio menus**: the audio clip menu in FL's two columns, the channel's Levels adjustment (read from and written to .flp), Track mode › Audio track with the list of mixer tracks (thanks to scottholdren), instrument tracks, the multilink menu, plugin A/B states and more of FL's settings.
**Gross Beat** slots can be triggered by MIDI notes and its Smooth points follow FL's curve. **Pitcher**'s MIDI mode and Harmonize take notes from its MIDI port.
**Stand-ins**: a project that uses a missing drum gate or a G3-style bus compressor opens with a closer LYNX SHARE effect.
**New logo**, by w3teal, in the app, the installers, the website and the Store.
fixed: The metronome count-in and its length were not saved, a recording could land on another mixer insert than the one chosen, and a VST3 knob moved by a MIDI controller did not move in the plugin's window. (#152)
Spectral Compressor and other plugins with a sidechain input crashed LYNX SHARE. On Linux and macOS a plugin that crashes while it plays is now switched off and LYNX SHARE keeps going. (#155)
Searching for missing files, such as a SoundFont on a slow disk, could freeze the window. (#159)
After an edit, every Piano roll note of a Fruity Slicer played the same slice. (#160)
Find similar samples could wait a long time for an answer on a busy computer.
known: .als export writes Drum Racks, but no Live has opened one yet. Live's devices with no LYNX SHARE equivalent (Hybrid Reverb, Grain Delay, Amp, Roar, FM Operator patches and others) are dropped on import and listed.
Some of Live's device settings follow assumed laws that have not been checked against Live yet, and a converted Live Reverb's wet signal is louder than Live's.
A 6/8 scene plays a three-beat bar.
The crash guard on Linux and macOS does not cover a plugin that crashes while opening its editor, loading a preset or on its own threads.
In FL Studio Mobile projects most DirectWave samples are not available, so most programs play a LYNX SHARE stand-in.

title: Simple workflow, racks and Clip View, Slicex and FPC, freeze, controller profiles
summary: A third layout, the Simple workflow, joins the Pattern and Clip-launch workflows. The Clip-launch side gains a Clip View, a Device View, racks, note chance and Live's MIDI tools. Slicex and FPC are instruments with FL Studio's editors, FL Studio Mobile projects come in with instruments, effects and automation, plugin windows dock, channels can be frozen and common MIDI controllers work from profiles.
new: **Simple workflow** (View › Layout style, and offered by the setup wizard): one window with the tracks and the timeline. The New track chooser adds a voice, an instrument, a sampler or a starter beat in one click, dropped loops keep time and the project has a key. The Finish dock gives the Master a ready-made sound and saves the song as WAV, MP3 or a package for other apps. The other windows stay one click away.

**Clip View, Device View and racks** (Clip-launch workflow): a selected clip opens with Clip, Launch and Notes panels and the Piano roll docked under the grid, and the selected track's effects show as a chain of cards. Instrument and Audio Effect Racks with chains, zones and macros open from Live sets and are written back, and a mixer slot's menu groups it into a rack. A MIDI Effect Rack can be built and is written to a Live set, but Live's own MIDI Effect Racks are not opened yet.

**Note chance and MIDI tools**: every note has a Chance and a Velocity range, and Live 12's probability groups are kept in .als sets. Live 12's MIDI tools (Arpeggiate, Chop, Connect, Ornament, Quantize, Recombine, Span, Strum, Time Warp and Velocity Shaper) are in the Clip View and in the Piano roll's Tools menu.
**Warp markers**: Auto-warp locks an audio clip to the beat, and markers can be added, moved and removed in the audio editor's warp lane. The Playlist shows them as flags on the clip.

**Slicex and FPC** are instruments with FL Studio's editor layout. FL's saved settings are read and written back, and both were compared with FL Studio's own renders. Fruity Slicer has its envelope page and voice settings, and a note-off ends its slice. (#74, #129, #135)

**FL Studio Mobile (.flm)**: MiniSynth, Transistor Bass, 3x Osc and GMSynth channels play on LYNX SHARE's engines, FL Studio Mobile's effects come in as the new Pocket effects, and level, pan, mute, solo, pitch bend and send moves become automation clips. (#88)

**Freeze** (right-click a channel in the Channel rack): the channel plays audio rendered from it and its instrument is unloaded, a third-party plugin included. Volume, pan and the insert's effects stay live, and Unfreeze brings back exactly what was there.

**Docked plugin windows**, as in FL Studio: plugin editors sit inside the main window like the other panels. Settings › General has FL's "Detach all new plugins", and Tools › Macros › Switch all plugin editors to chooses Attached or Detached for all of them. A detached window can be pinned on top. (#116)

**MIDI controller profiles** (Settings › MIDI › Controller type): Mackie Control with its extender, Launchkey MK3, APC Key 25 mk2, KeyLab Essential mk3 and nanoKONTROL2, with soft takeover and feedback to the device. **MPE**, first stage: an MPE controller plays each note with its own bend, timbre and pressure, and a third-party plugin can receive MPE. (#108)

**Online sessions**: the host can share plugins with the guests. A shared plugin runs on the host's computer and a guest changes its settings from their own window, without owning it. A guest whose LYNX SHARE restarts goes back in as the same person, and Linux can host a session.

**Projects**: File › Versions... lists a project's saved versions and backups. A project can be opened without its third-party plugins, your own default template opens at start-up and with File › New (#123), and Export can write one file per marker section and keep named presets.

**Tools**: Convert to MIDI turns the melody, harmony or drums of an audio clip into a pattern, on your own computer. Piano roll scripts run FL Studio's .pyscript files (Tools › Scripts). The Browser finds samples similar to the one you right-click. Strike Shaper is a new transient designer (#94), and a loudness meter (LUFS and true peak) can sit beside the Master.
better: **Playlist**, as in FL Studio: Edit and Select menus, Shift+arrow keys and Alt+Left / Right move clips (#147), fade and gain handles have menus with Create crossfade and Normalize, and there are Make unique as sample, Magic lasso and optional levels and controls on track headers. Pattern Blocks have pencil, brush and eraser tools (#127).

**Mixer**: deleting mixer tracks asks first, as in FL Studio. Links to a deleted insert can be kept and shown greyed, inserts can be arranged like the Playlist and a send can be pre-fader. A muted insert keeps its meter moving and keeps running its effects, as in FL Studio (#144).

**Plugins**: Processing › Connections sends an instrument's outputs to separate mixer inserts (#114). Third-party plugins in FL Studio projects play at FL's level (they were 3 dB quieter). A crashed plugin can be reloaded without reopening the project, LYNX SHARE's keys work while a plugin window has focus (#96), and VST3 parameter menus offer LYNX SHARE's automation items.
**Piano roll**: a Keyboard style option with traditional piano keys, a Chord stamp list, FL Studio's vertical zoom wheel, and Snap to scale moves notes by scale steps.

**Recording and MIDI**: sustain and sostenuto pedals hold notes, and a Layer passes the pedal on to its channels (#141). There are Tools › Cancel recording, an optional "Low latency while recording" switch and 16-bit disk recording.
**Render to audio** plays at the level of the insert it replaces (it was about 5 dB louder). Pattern renders and consolidated clips do too.

**Effects**: Crest, Sentry, Ember, Nebula, Halo, Foil Plate, Atrium, Epoch Verb, Echoform and Horizon were refitted against the tools they are modelled on. LYNX Tune has Breathiness (#103). When a project uses a third-party compressor, limiter, saturator or gate that is not installed, LYNX SHARE's stand-in loads with matching settings for more of them.

**LYNX extras** (Settings): one page with LYNX SHARE's own additions that are off by default, such as the loudness meter beside the Master and automation lanes under Playlist tracks. Preview in time (in the Browser's menu) and "Muted inserts don't process" (in the Mixer's menu) are new options too. The plugin database is now a folder you can arrange in the file manager (#104), and LYNX Dance loads sprite sheets made for Fruity Dance (#121).
**Compressor** has a FET voicing next to the clean one, and **Apex Limiter** has a levelling stage under the ceiling (off by default).
fixed: A mixer track with a Patcher that holds a Fruity Limiter played about 1000 samples late compared with FL Studio. (#113)
Recording into a looping pattern clip folded the take over itself (#126), and an automation clip took a control back from a MIDI controller while you moved it (#125).
Changing the audio device while a project played could crash LYNX SHARE, and opening a Windows Audio device could take more than a minute on some devices. (#134)
Third-party plugins in imported FL Studio projects could be silenced by FL's cut groups. Surge XT was one. (#143)
A project opened over another one could keep the first project's settings for a plugin they both use.
An audio clip on a Sampler channel was silent, and an export could start before a SoundFont had finished loading (#138).
Linux: LYNX SHARE crashed at start on systems without a monospaced font (#142), and Linux could not host a live session. Samples in FL Studio's Shared data and Downloads folders are found (#124).
Mod X and Mod Y move the Sampler's filter, and a note's fine pitch reaches third-party plugins. (#63)
known: Freeze works on instrument channels only, not on mixer inserts. The notes of a frozen channel cannot be edited until you Unfreeze it.

MPE is a first stage: one value of bend, timbre and pressure is recorded per note, not a curve. Of the built-in instruments, the Sampler, FPC and the built-in synth follow it, and the others do not yet. It has not been tried with a real MPE controller yet.
The controller profiles were written from each device's documentation and have not been tried on the hardware yet.
Harmless can play up to about 1.7 dB louder or quieter after a rest, depending on the audio buffer size.
LYNX Dance keeps Fruity Dance's "On desktop" option for FL Studio projects, but it does nothing: dancers stay in the main window.

.flm import: instruments other than MiniSynth, Transistor Bass, 3x Osc, GMSynth, DirectWave and the samplers play the built-in synth, and a .dwp missing from FL Studio's copy of the FLM resources plays a stand-in.

Live set export: LYNX SHARE's own instruments and effects are not converted (their tracks and notes are kept), and effect-parameter automation and insert-to-insert routes are dropped. On import, Live's own effects are dropped.
A plugin in a separate process, or in the 32-bit bridge, opens its editor in its own window and cannot be docked or pinned.

title: Ableton Live sets, FL Studio Mobile import, 32-bit plugins
summary: LYNX SHARE opens and exports Ableton Live sets (.als), imports FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) and loads 32-bit plugins on Windows. It also adds video tracks with ADR, VCA faders, automation lanes and modulators, loop-take comping and an optional Clip-launch layout.
new: **Ableton Live sets (.als)**: File › Open reads Live 11 and 12 sets, and File › Export › Ableton Live set (.als) writes them for Live 11 or 12 with the samples copied into the set's project folder. Import brings MIDI, audio, group and return tracks, tempo, locators, mixer settings with their automation and VST2 / VST3 plugins with their state; Simpler / Sampler and drum racks become LYNX SHARE samplers, and Live's other devices are listed in the import report.

**FL Studio Mobile (.flm)**: File › Open imports the arrangement, samples, drum kits and DirectWave programs, with rack levels, pan and routes. Samples are searched next to the .flm and in FL Studio's copy of the FLM resources; missing ones go to the Missing files window.
**32-bit VST2 / VST3 plugins on Windows**: they run through a bridge (`LYNX-bridge32.exe`) that adds no latency. A plugin that crashes in the bridge stops on its own while LYNX SHARE keeps playing.

**Video tracks and ADR**: video clips on the Playlist with a SMPTE ruler, frame-by-frame moves, Extract the sound and Export with video (needs FFmpeg). For dialogue replacement there is a cue list with streamers, beeps and take comping. (#83)

**Clip-launch workflow** (View › Layout style, optional): a clip grid with scenes next to the Playlist, with launch modes, quantisation, legato, loop and follow actions. Live sets bring their Session clips into it and export writes them back; the default Pattern workflow is unchanged.

**VCA faders and folding mixer groups**: Group › VCA › New VCA from selected makes a VCA that can be automated and nested. Groups fold to their bus strip, and any effect with a side input has a Sidechain from picker in one menu.

**Comping**: each pass of an audio loop recording lands on its own Playlist track, in a group. Comp these takes (right-click a track of the group) adds a comp track; drag across the take lanes to pick parts, then audition, crossfade and flatten.

**Automation lanes and modulators**: optional automation lanes under Playlist tracks (off by default), and Tools › Modulators... adds an LFO or random source that moves a knob around its own value. Multilink to controllers (Ctrl+J) links the controls you move to the controllers you move next, as in FL Studio.
better: **Mixer routing stays put**: moving, inserting or deleting mixer tracks keeps sends, sidechains, Fruity Send, Transmitter, Patcher and Voltage Controller outputs, automation and MIDI links on their track.

**Export to FL Studio**: the exported project renders at the right length (FL's Thief demo came out at 8:12 instead of 3:59.9), and LYNX SHARE-only instruments rendered to audio play at unity in FL Studio (about 5 dB too loud before). Muted Playlist clips are written muted instead of being left out (#110), and clip fades are written so FL Studio plays them.

**Stretched samples follow FL's TIME knob**: precomputed effects and Trim are applied first, then only the span that plays is stretched. In FL's Thief demo the ride cymbal played about 3x too fast; projects that combine TIME with Trim, a precomputed fade or a Start / Length region may sound different from before.

**Plugins in a separate process**: this works on macOS too, and the plugin window does not float over other apps. Keys the plugin window does not use (Space, F-keys, your shortcuts) reach LYNX SHARE, and Esc closes the window. (#99)

**Linux**: LV2 plugins are scanned once in one helper process; with 510 plugins the first scan went from 25 minutes to about 12 s (#85), and a plugin that crashes the scan is blacklisted (#90). The interface font is Open Sans, bundled, because labels were cut short with wider distribution fonts; Settings › General › Interface font picks any installed font.
fixed: A plugin crashing in its own window closed LYNX SHARE on Windows. A message offers Save as... and Always run in a separate process instead. (#32)
Third-party plugins with a side input get the slot's sidechain source, and the side input is on only while a source feeds it. Plugins such as RCompressor compress again. (#109)
Audio tracks lost their mixer link when a project was reopened. (#122)
known: Render to audio (an insert bounced to an audio clip) plays about 5 dB louder than the insert it replaces. A fix is planned.

Live set export: LYNX SHARE's own instruments and effects are not converted (their tracks and notes are kept), effect-parameter automation and insert-to-insert routes are dropped, and Live trims overlapping audio clips. Live set import: racks keep their first chain, and Live's own effects are dropped.
.flm import: FLM's effects are not imported yet, and a .dwp missing from FL Studio's copy of the FLM resources plays a stand-in.
With several overlapping automation clips on one control, LYNX SHARE's choice can differ from FL Studio's. At a clip's start LYNX SHARE reaches the new value in about 8 ms, where FL Studio glides.
A 32-bit or bridged plugin's editor opens in its own window.
A tempo moved by a linked MIDI controller does not resize audio clips. Type or set the final tempo.

title: Export to FL Studio, live online sessions, plugin picker
summary: A song can be exported as an FL Studio project, and online sessions are live, with reconnect, chat and permissions. Harmor and Sytrus have new editors, F8 opens a plugin picker with pictures, the toolbar was reworked and several of LYNX SHARE's own effects were refitted against the tools they are modelled on.
new: **Export to FL Studio** (File › Export › FL Studio project...): saves the song as an FL Studio 2026 project, either a .flp or a zipped loop package with every sample. Samplers, audio clips, FL's own generators and effects and VST2 / VST3 / CLAP plugins go over with their settings; anything only LYNX SHARE has is rendered to audio or swapped for the nearest FL plugin, and a report lists what happened to each part.

**Live online sessions**: a guest whose connection drops reconnects and keeps their edits, and if the host's LYNX SHARE closes, the next start offers to resume the session. There is a session chat, guests can follow the host's transport, the host can change what each person may edit, and parts that use a plugin someone does not have are rendered by the person who has it and streamed as audio.

**Plugin picker** (F8, as in FL Studio): every generator and effect shown as a picture of its own editor, with categories as tabs. Type to search, double-click or press Enter to add, or drag one onto the Channel rack or a mixer slot.
**Pattern Blocks**: FL's classic playlist, with one row per pattern next to the clip tracks. Paint with left-click, erase with right-click, and turn the blocks into clips when you are done. (#60)

**Patcher parameter ports**: right-click a node › Inputs / Outputs › Parameters, then drag a Surface knob onto a parameter to drive it live. This works for plugins too, and FL Patcher presets bring their ports along. (#65)

**Capture MIDI** (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+R): saves the last phrase you played without recording. Recording also keeps the chord played right on the downbeat after the count-in, and MIDI notes are timed to the sample.
better: **Harmor and Sytrus editors**: Harmor has a new editor in FL's section order, with part A and part B pages, a Global strip with the X / Y / Z pad and an FX panel; part B and the global settings can be edited. Sytrus shows FL's FM / RM modulation matrix.

**Toolbar**: bigger icons and buttons, a large song position, master volume and pitch as two knobs, and a magnet to switch snap on and off. The recording switches sit side by side, with new Loop record, Step edit (Ctrl+E), Punch in/out, Blend (Ctrl+B) and a tempo tapper.

**Mixer and plugin menus**: several selected mixer tracks can be routed at once, effect slots are fixed places as FL's 10 slots are, and plugin menus are listed A to Z under FL's categories, where a letter key jumps to the next plugin starting with it (#64). Dragging a mixer fader during playback keeps up with the mouse instead of stalling the meters.

**Effects closer to the originals**: Apex Limiter, Crest Compressor, Sentry Gate, Hush De-esser and Prism Multiband were refitted; LuxeVerb gains a Space page, Ridge Strip a Modern console voicing and Ember Saturator a Classic panel. Aether's Mid Air is audible again (#77).

**FL generators and projects**: every new FL generator starts like a new one in FL Studio when FL Studio is installed. Transistor Bass, FL Slayer, BooBass and DrumSynth Live accept FL 2025's files too, and Drumaxx, FPC, Slicex and Transistor Bass play at FL's level.
fixed: VST3 instruments cut chords off. Each note carries its own note ID, as FL Studio does. (#70)
Parametric EQ lost FL presets after save and reopen. Every setting of every built-in effect is saved exactly, inside Patcher too. (#67)
Detached windows come back detached, at their own place and size. (#62)
Linux file choosers: when the system dialog cannot open, LYNX SHARE uses its own file chooser, and upper-case extensions are listed. (#72)
Notes were left hanging after deleting, moving or lengthening them while they play, and Playlist clicks could land about two bars early. (#32)

title: Project packages for friends, designed plugin editors, Microsoft Store
summary: A project can be sent to a friend as one file and their part merged back. Nearly 40 FL plugins that opened as a plain knob grid have editors laid out like FL's, the Mixer has FL's eight layouts and track icons, and LYNX SHARE is on the Microsoft Store.
new: **Send a project to a friend** (File › Online session): the project travels as one `.lynxpack` file with every sample and audio renders of the parts that use third-party plugins. Your friend records their part and uses Send my part back..., you add it with Merge a part..., and one Undo takes it out again; up to 4 people per project, no account or server needed. The live version is not in this release.
**Microsoft Store**: LYNX SHARE is available on the Microsoft Store for Windows. The Store version updates through the Store.

**Mixer layouts and track icons**: FL's eight layouts in the Mixer's title bar, from Compact to Extra large, kept per user. Mixer tracks, channels and Playlist tracks can have an icon (Change icon...), and FL projects keep theirs. (#52)

**Record an insert after its effects**: FL's six Record positions in the insert's input menu (Post EQ by default), with the effects' latency taken out. The dry input can also be recorded as a second take, for re-amping. (#41)

**Render and export**: Patterns › Quick render, Render as audio clip and Render and replace, Consolidate playlist selection (Ctrl+Alt+C), Export all playlist tracks, Project bones and Export › Master... (Ctrl+Alt+M), which masters to a loudness target on your computer.

**LYNX SHARE preset banks**: Toxic Biohazard, PoiZone, Harmless, DX10, SimSynth, BeepMap, Granulizer, Fruit Kick, Drumpad, Sakura and others have presets that work without FL Studio. The preset arrows step through LYNX SHARE's presets, your own, then FL's when FL Studio is installed.
better: **Designed plugin editors**: Toxic Biohazard, PoiZone, Harmless, Ogun, GMS, Morphine, Kepler, Transistor Bass, Sawer, Sakura, FL Slayer, Love Philter, Peak Controller and about 25 more open in FL's own layout, drawn in LYNX SHARE's style. LYNX SHARE's own effects (EQ, Delay, Reverb, Limiter and more) show what the setting does, such as the frequency response or the echoes on the beat grid.

**Maximus In/Out graph can be edited** with FL's gestures: right-click to add a point, drag points and curve handles, Alt+right-click to delete. It is saved in FL's format and the sound follows the curve. (#40)
**Typing keyboard to piano** is in Options (Ctrl+T) under FL's name, on by default and at FL's octave. Right-click its button for Root note and Octave. (#34)

**Playlist and Piano roll**: Alt+M / Shift+Alt+M mute and unmute the selected clips (#53), and a STRETCH button (Shift+M) makes resizing an audio clip stretch it. The Piano roll gets note grid highlights (Alt+B), a background waveform (Alt+N), FL score files (.fsc) and the MIDI clipboard shared with FL Studio.
**Linux AppImage updates in place** with Gear Lever or AppImageUpdate. (#48)
fixed: macOS: LYNX SHARE closed a few seconds after launch when a folder in the Browser held a file name macOS cannot read as text. (#42)
u-he CLAP plugins (Presswerk) crashed LYNX SHARE after asking for a restart, also during export. (#46)
Moving a mixer effect slot, track or channel reset the plugin's settings, and reordering slots with Presswerk crashed on Linux. (#36)
Multi-monitor menus: submenus stay on the menu's own display, and on Linux menus in the main window open again while a panel is undocked. (#45)
With the loop region on, each pass played one sample too many, so long loops drifted off the beat. Fit to tempo also keeps a loop's exact length instead of stretching it to a power of two. (#32)

title: Stem extraction, looping pattern clips, FL's MIDI Out
summary: Extract stems from sample splits an audio clip into drums, bass, instruments and vocals on your own computer. Stretched pattern clips loop their pattern, Song-mode recording keeps every bar, MIDI Out works like FL's, and FL projects open closer to how they were saved.
new: **Extract stems from sample** (Playlist, audio clip menu): splits the clip's sample into drums, bass, instruments and vocals, each on a new track under the clip. It uses the HT-Demucs model (166 MB), downloaded on first use only if you agree; your audio never leaves your computer, and a 3-minute song takes about 2.5 minutes on a 6-core PC with about 4 GB of memory at peak. (#31)
**SFZ instruments** play in the LYNX Soundfont channel, with round robin, release triggers, choke groups, key switches and loops. Samples can be WAV, FLAC, OGG, AIFF or MP3. (#22)

**Gross Beat with slots, presets and an editable envelope**: a LYNX SHARE factory bank (25 time and 30 volume slots, 29 presets) and FL's envelope gestures. Edits are heard right away and saved in FL's Gross Beat format.
**Mono, Porta and Slide on every instrument** (Channel settings › Misc): FL engines, the drums, the Sampler and VST / VST3 / CLAP plugins. Imported FL projects keep these settings.
**FL's mixer presets**: File › States lists FL's mixer presets, your FL ones and LYNX SHARE states, and loads them onto the selected tracks.
better: **Stretched pattern clips loop their pattern**: in 0.1.21 the repeats were only drawn; they are played, also in export. FL Studio plays such a clip once, so this is a LYNX SHARE extra; turn it off in Options › General for FL's behaviour. (#25)
**Song-mode recording keeps every bar you play**: before, notes folded into the pattern's first bar or two. Each note stays where you played it, the pattern grows and its clip covers the take.

**MIDI Out is FL's MIDI Out**: channel, General MIDI patch list, bank and port, plus 8 renameable pages of 3 x 3 knobs that can each be a CC, RPN, NRPN, aftertouch or note. FL's 41 presets load, and FL projects keep their pages. (#17)
**Channel rack**: Insert, Replace and + list the same generators, so Replace can swap in FL engines, VFX, Patcher, Sampler and plugins while keeping the channel's notes and insert. (#18)

**Mixer pan works like FL's** (the panned-away side folds into the other one), with Options › Project › Panning law (Circular / Triangular). Alt solo (Alt+S) plays the selected tracks with the tracks that feed them.

**More of FL's keys**: F10 / F11 close on a second press (#23), Ctrl + middle-drag zooms the Piano roll vertically (#26), Playlist keys 7 / 8 / 9 pitch or reverse the selected audio clips, and Ctrl+Z toggles undo / redo the way FL's does. On macOS, Cmd does what Ctrl does.
**FL engines**: Transporter, Wave Traveller, Kepler Exo and Emphasis run on FL's own engines, bit-identical with FL Studio. Newtime plays FL's warp markers and is out of beta.

**FL projects open as saved**: main pitch, the open pattern, PAT / SONG mode, sample start / end regions (they used to play the wrong part), per-clip stretch, clip pitch / reverse and the panning law. The Sampler's precomputed effects (normalize, reverse, fades, crossfade, trim) and declicking modes are kept too.
fixed: A CLAP plugin asking for a restart could be restarted mid-block and crash. (#29)
A damaged SF3 SoundFont could crash LYNX SHARE while loading or previewing. (#30)
Fewer dropouts at playback start with Reeverb 2, Fruity Reeverb, Stereo Enhancer / Shaper, Fruity Delay 2 and Harmless.

title: In-app updates, 500 mixer inserts, automatic crossfades
summary: LYNX SHARE updates itself: a bar says when a new version is out and Update installs it. The requests from issues #14, #15 and #16 are in, checked against FL Studio 2026. From 0.1.20 or older, install 0.1.21 by hand once.
new: **In-app updates**: a few seconds after start LYNX SHARE checks GitHub for a newer version and shows a slim bar under the toolbar with What's new and Update. On Windows (installer) Update downloads the installer, checks its SHA-256 and installs over itself; the portable zip and macOS get the download in your Downloads folder, and the Linux AppImage updates in place when AppImageUpdate is installed. The check sends nothing about you and can be turned off in Settings › General › Updates.
**Up to 500 mixer inserts**, like FL Studio 2026's dynamic mixer (was 127). Insert multiple... and the + button's right-click menu say how many more fit. (#14)

**Piano roll: ghost channels and Fold to the scale**: right-click the ghost notes button to choose, channel by channel, whose notes show as ghosts. Note tools › Fold to the scale shows only the keys of the chosen scale (LYNX SHARE's own). (#14)

**Playlist: automatic crossfades**, as in FL 2026: where two audio clips on a track overlap, they crossfade over the whole overlap, so the level stays even. It is switched per project in Settings › Project › Playlist; projects saved before keep it off. (#16)

**Playlist: clip gain handle**: hover an audio clip and drag the small half circle at the bottom centre to change that clip's volume, independently of the channel volume. Right-click the handle for Reset gain, Normalize and Type in value. (#16)

**Plugin folders in the Mixer and Channel rack menus**, as in FL 2026: in the Browser's Plugin database, right-click a plugin › Move to folder. The add menus then list each folder under its own heading, and the folder layout you made in FL Studio can be copied (read only). (#16)

**Parametric EQ 2 shows the spectrum, with FL's heatmap**: the graph draws the spectrum of the EQ's output. Right-click an empty spot of the graph › Heatmap colours every frequency column from cold violet to hot orange. (#16)

**Facet EQ: comparative EQ**: an EQ / Source / Target switch lets you hear the EQ, the track without it, or another track, level-matched by default. The same menu can draw the target's spectrum over yours and build a Match EQ toward it. (#16)
better: **LYNX Tune**: Throat length (50 to 180 %), Transpose in scale, and Amplitude, Formant and Variation for the created vibrato. Auto-Tune Pro and EFX+ settings in imported projects carry these values over; existing projects sound as before.
**Piano roll note entry**: Alt+wheel changes the velocity of all selected notes wherever the mouse is, and new notes copy the velocity and pan of the last clicked note, as in FL Studio. (#16)
fixed: **Audio clips keep the mixer insert you give them**: moving one audio clip used to send its channel back to the insert of whatever audio track it touched. Only a clip moved onto another audio track takes that track's insert, as in FL Studio. (#15)
**Piano roll: snap to scale moves every dragged note**: dragging several notes up or down used to move only the note you grabbed. (#14)
The Piano roll keyboard lights up the keys of the sounding notes while the song plays or while you play a MIDI keyboard. (#14)

**Master pitch, channel pitch and slide notes on every instrument**: slide notes glide on FL's native instruments, and VST / VST3 / CLAP instruments get the channel's PITCH knob, fine tune and master pitch as MIDI pitch bend. (#14)
Facet EQ: a press on or near a bell always moves the bell; the range handle used to catch the click. (#16)
Echoform went silent with the feedback at the top and a very short time on the tape voicings.

title: New name, 15 languages, Performance mode, VFX Script, Edison tools
summary: LYNX is now LYNX SHARE, and the interface is in 15 languages. The open issues were re-checked against FL Studio 2026 and most differences fixed to match it; the release also adds Performance mode, MIDI sync, Python VFX scripts, Edison's tools in the audio editor and several FL plugins.
new: **LYNX is now LYNX SHARE**: the repository moved (old links keep working). Settings, presets, plugin list and projects stay where they are, and updating over an existing install works as before.

**15 languages**: besides English and Portuguese (Brazil), the interface is in Spanish, French, German, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean and Chinese (Simplified and Traditional). Settings › Language lists them, and on the first start LYNX SHARE picks your system language when it is one of them.

**Performance mode** (Playlist › Options › Performance mode, Ctrl+P): put a Start marker where the song begins and the clips before it become a launch grid, with FL's per-track press, follow and sync settings. Clips can be launched from a MIDI controller and a performance recorded into the arrangement; FL projects made for Performance mode open with it on.

**VFX Script runs Python scripts**: an embedded Python interpreter and an `flvfx` module run FL's VFX Script presets (all 89 factory presets load and run) and your own note scripts. Scripts run off the audio thread with a time and memory limit, so a runaway script stops with a message.

**Audio editor: FL Edison's tools**: Amp, Equalizer, Match spectrum, Blur, Convolution reverb, Clean up (denoiser, declipper, declicker), Vocal denoiser / isolator, Drum(loop) stretcher, Loop tuner and the Time stretcher / pitch shifter, each with Preview and one undo step. Volume, panning and stereo separation envelopes can be drawn over the audio.

**MIDI sync** (Settings › MIDI): Send master sync to any MIDI output device as MIDI clock with Song Position Pointer or as MIDI Time Code, with a per-device offset, so drum machines and other programs follow LYNX SHARE's tempo and position. LYNX SHARE can also follow an incoming MIDI clock (External sync).

**New FL plugins**: Fruity Video Player (a video in sync with the song, decoded by your own ffmpeg), Transmitter (FL Studio 2026's transient / sustain splitter), Fruity Scratcher, Fruity Mute 2, Fruity Big Clock, Tuner and Fruity HTML NoteBook. They also come in from FL projects.

**Channel rack looping (polyrhythms)**: the loop button in the Channel rack title lets a channel shorter than the pattern repeat to its end, for example a 3-step hat against a 16-step kick. Burn to pattern writes the repeats into real notes, and FL projects import their loop settings.
better: **Automation clip point editing**: right-click inside an automation clip adds a point, right-click a point opens its menu, and the tension handles bend the segments, as in FL Studio. Before, right-clicking inside a clip deleted the whole clip. Fruity WaveShaper's curve can be edited with the mouse too. (#11)

**Knobs and effect windows follow their automation**: while the song plays, automated faders, knobs and the built-in effect windows (Parametric EQ 2's bands, Fruity Filter, Delay, Reeverb, Facet EQ) show the automated values. Grab one with the mouse and your hand wins while you hold it. (#11, #12)

**FL engines out of beta**: Fruity Granulizer, Newtone and Kepler are out of beta after being checked against FL's renders. Every Harmor factory preset plays on Harmor's own engine (the 88 presets saved by its first versions were refused before).

**Faster**: time-stretched samples are kept in a disk cache, so opening a project again does not stretch them again (FL's Thief demo: 6.2 s down to 3.8 s on a second open). The mixer uses more cores, with render CPU time about 10 to 20 % lower on busy projects and the same output.
fixed: **Shift+Space works as in FL 2026**: while playing or recording it stops at the start of the song (or of the time selection); when stopped it plays from the current position. (#11)
Crashes: cycling quickly through samples (#12) and opening the ASIO driver's control panel from Settings › Audio (#12, #13). The buffer size picked in the driver's own panel is kept.

**Shortcuts**: a key you set yourself always wins over the Playlist's or Piano roll's built-in tool keys, and Space, the F-keys and your own shortcuts work with LYNX SHARE's other windows in front. (#12)

**Linux: drag and drop of audio files from the file manager** through the XWayland bridges of GNOME and KDE. GNOME 50's mutter itself does not pass Wayland drags to XWayland windows; mutter 51.1 fixes that. (#11)
known: Harmor keeps its (beta) mark: 6 of its 325 presets still sound different from FL Studio.
Newtime stays in beta: FL's own time warping is not reproduced yet.
Fruity Scratcher: DVS timecode input is not reproduced. Transmitter: sends of the transient / sustain parts to other tracks are not routed yet (the import report lists them).
Recording pitch bend from a real MIDI controller could not be checked before release; playback of recorded bends is tested.

title: FL's VFX note effects, Layer, controllers, Hardware Insert, Visualizer
summary: This release adds what 0.1.18 left out: FL's VFX note effects, Layer, the X-Y controllers, Dashboard and Voltage Controller, the Wave Candy analyzer, a Visualizer with video export and a Hardware Insert for outboard gear. It also fixes pitched audio clips from FL projects and the start of exports.
new: **FL's VFX note effects**: Key Mapper, Color Mapper, Level Scaler, Keyboard Splitter, Envelope and Sequencer work as note processors inside a Patcher or on a Channel rack channel (Add › VFX (note effects)). FL's factory presets load from FL Studio's folder, and .flp projects that use them import with their settings.

**Layer channel**: a Layer makes no sound of its own; every note it gets plays its children (select channels in the Channel rack, then Set children). Random, Sequential and Crossfade modes and per-child key ranges work, and .flp projects with layers import with them.

**X-Y and X-Y-Z Controllers, Control Surface and Dashboard**: FL's controller plugins with their own editors. Every output can drive any knob (right-click it › Link to internal controller), and FL projects that use them import with their links working.

**Voltage Controller**: FL's control-voltage generator, for modular synths through a DC-coupled audio interface. Notes become pitch (1 V or 1.2 V per octave), gate, trigger, velocity or clock voltages.

**Hardware Insert**: a mixer effect that sends the insert's signal to the audio-interface outputs you pick and brings it back from the inputs your gear is wired to. Ping measures the round trip and LYNX SHARE delays every other track to match.

**Wave Candy and Visualizer**: two mixer effects that show the sound without changing it. Wave Candy has an oscilloscope, spectrum, spectrogram, peak / RMS / VU / LUFS meters and a vectorscope; Visualizer draws audio-reactive scenes and exports a video of the whole song (an MP4 when ffmpeg is installed, otherwise PNG frames and a WAV).

**Browser folders window**: the options button beside the Browser's search box › Show folders... opens a window to tick the folders you want to see and add your own. With a Show filter on (for example Audio files only), folders that hold nothing of that kind are left out of the tree.
better: **Patcher**: double-clicking a Synth, Sampler or FL-engine node opens the same editor it has on a channel. A plugin node that outputs MIDI (an arpeggiator, a MIDI effect) gets a MIDI out pin that can be cabled to instruments.
fixed: **FL projects: pitched audio clips play at the right pitch**: an audio clip's channel pitch, root note and the Sampler's Time stretching PITCH knob come over from FL Studio as FL plays them.
**Export: the start of the song could be missing**: the first moments (up to about two seconds) were sometimes rendered as silence.

Fixed-size windows (Settings, New project, Export audio and others) that are taller than the screen at 150 to 200 % zoom or on small laptop screens scroll inside, so their buttons are always reachable.
Mod wheel, other CCs, channel aftertouch and pitch wheel played into a Patcher channel reach the plugins cabled to its notes; before, only the notes got through.
A Formula Controller (or any controller) on an insert with no audio froze after a second of silence.
known: VFX Script keeps its Python script and settings but does not run them yet: its notes pass through unchanged.
Hardware Insert: exports pass the dry signal (the Export window says so). Record the return to keep the gear's sound.

title: Audio recording tools, Browser filters, themes, clean mixer
summary: Audio recording gets sample-accurate takes, a round-trip measurement, punch in/out, loop takes with comping and recordings that survive a crash. The Browser gets filters, a search index and a separate Sample browser, and there are themes, plugin presets and a clean mixer option, plus the fixes from issues #7, #8 and #9.
new: **Sample-accurate recording and round-trip measurement**: recorded audio lands on the Playlist exactly where you played it (the clip start could be up to about half a millisecond off before). In Options › Audio › Recording latency compensation, connect an output to an input with a cable and press Measure the round trip; LYNX SHARE uses the result for every recording on that device setup.

**One-key recording, punch in/out, pre-roll and post-roll**: Shift+R arms the selected mixer insert, records and plays; Shift+R again stops. In the record menu, punch in/out records only the Playlist's time selection, with playback starting and stopping a set number of bars around it.

**Loop takes and comping**: recording audio over a loop region gives one clip per pass; the last one plays and the earlier ones go muted on folded lanes under the track. Right-click a take › Promote this take to the comp track builds the best take from pieces.

**Recordings survive a crash**: takes are saved to disk every second while recording, and the next start offers to put recovered recordings back on the Playlist. LYNX SHARE also warns when the disk has less than 10 minutes of recording left.

**Browser search index, filters and Sample browser**: searches read an index kept between sessions, so results show at once. The options button beside the search box chooses which folders and file kinds are listed, and View › Sample browser (separate window) opens a second, independent Browser for samples.

**Themes** (Options › Theme): change the accent color, the background and the workspace behind the panels, which can be an image. Six built-in presets, your own presets, and import/export of `.lynxtheme` files; the Rename and color dialogs also get a color wheel.

**Plugin presets**: the plugin window has preset arrows and a Presets menu with the plugin's own presets, your presets, Save preset... and Load / Export preset file... (`.lynxpreset`, VST2 `.fxp`/`.fxb`, VST3 `.vstpreset`). Saved presets also appear in the Browser under Plugin presets.

**Clean mixer and new-project setup**: Options › Mixer › Clean mixer takes the built-in 3-band EQ off every insert (your EQ settings are kept). The same page sets how many inserts new projects start with (0 to 125), the Master chain in new projects, and Show only used inserts.

**Pitch... for samples and audio clips**: right-click a sample channel or an audio clip › Pitch...: semitones, cents and Keep length. Without Keep length the sample is resampled like tape (higher is shorter).

**Patcher and Envelope Controller**: the Patcher's Add plugin menu is laid out in columns by category like FL's and lists the controllers, MIDI Out, every FL engine and effect and your VST plugins; From LYNX / To LYNX nodes have MIDI ports 0 to 255. The Envelope Controller editor gets LFO, Keyboard, Velocity, Modulation X / Y and Random sections, and FL presets import with them.
better: **Follow on/off**: a Follow button in the Playlist and Piano roll toolbars. Off, the view stays where you scrolled while the song plays.

**Compact menus and 150 % zoom**: right-click and drop-down menus are about as tight as Windows' own menus (Options › General › Menu density › Comfortable brings back the roomier look). A window bigger than the screen shrinks or moves so its title bar and close button stay on screen.
fixed: Browser search crashed or froze LYNX SHARE when searching all folders on big drives.
Channels can be routed to any mixer insert, not just 1 to 16: the channel's track box goes up to insert 127 and the missing inserts are added.
Pitch wheel, mod wheel, other CCs and channel pressure go to the channel you play by default; plugins get them, and LYNX SHARE's Sampler and Synth bend by the channel's Misc › Pitch range.
Long recordings lost or shifted audio when the disk was slow: a recording could silently skip blocks and everything after them moved earlier.

title: Native PipeWire driver, separate-process plugins on Linux
summary: A Linux release: a native PipeWire driver with real-time priority without root, plugins in a separate process (also Windows plugins through yabridge), cheaper drawing and the AppImage in the applications menu.
new: **Native PipeWire driver** (Options › Audio settings › Driver › PipeWire (native)): chosen automatically on the first start when PipeWire runs, then JACK, then ALSA. It works at 32 to 2048 samples, shares the device with other programs, follows the output picked in your desktop's sound settings and shows up as `LYNX` in pw-link, qpwgraph or Helvum.

**Real-time priority without root**: LYNX SHARE asks for real-time scheduling for its audio threads (audio-group limits, RealtimeKit or the desktop portal). Options › Audio settings shows whether it got it, and if the sound breaks up without it LYNX SHARE explains once how to enable it.

**Plugins in a separate process on Linux**: Options › Plugins › Run plugins in a separate process works on Linux, checked with VST3 and LV2 plugins and with Windows plugins through yabridge. A plugin that crashes or freezes is muted and LYNX SHARE keeps running.

**AppImage in the applications menu**: the setup wizard (and Options › General) can add the AppImage to your applications menu and open `.lynx` files with it. From a terminal: `--menu-entry on` / `off`.
better: **Windows plugins through yabridge**: checked with yabridge 5.1.1 and Wine 10.0; scanning, the plugin window, playback, export and the separate process all work.
**Faster drawing on Linux**: knobs and rounded panels are drawn from cached images, so the Mixer is up to 8x cheaper to draw while playing, and the Mixer and Playlist scroll smoothly in big projects.
Linux crash files name the signal and list the crashing thread's frames, so crash reports from Linux are useful.

title: SoundFont player, new time-stretch, crash reports, hardware outputs
summary: A native SoundFont player, a new time-stretch engine, exact 16/24-bit exports and opt-in crash reports. It also fixes the Parametric EQ freeze and bad-sounding MP3s, lets you sing live through imported FL Studio projects and adds more of FL's Piano roll and Playlist tools.
new: **LYNX Soundfont**: a native SoundFont player (`.sf2` and `.sf3`) modelled on FL's Fruity Soundfont Player, with a preset search across all your SoundFonts. .flp projects with Fruity Soundfont Player import it with its font, preset, settings and automation. (#6)

**Crash reports (opt-in)**: after a crash or freeze, LYNX SHARE asks at the next start whether to send a report; you can see what will be sent first, skip it, or open a prefilled GitHub bug report instead. Reports carry no audio, projects, file names, user or computer name, and the server keeps no IP address.
**Hardware outputs**: each mixer insert (and the Master) can be routed to any output of your audio interface, including a single mono channel. This is imported from .flp.
**Plugin picker**: a searchable window with Instruments / Effects tabs, favorites, categories and vendors replaces the huge plugin submenu.

**Piano roll and Playlist tools**: 16 note colors, note groups (Shift+G / Alt+G), a Select menu and a chord readout in the Piano roll. In the Playlist: draw notes directly on instrument tracks, Detect tempo for audio clips and per-clip pan.
**Patcher**: a minimap, and a Surface tab with knobs, sliders, buttons and XY pads you can cable to the map.
better: **Time-stretch**: samples that follow the tempo, FL Stretch channels, Newtone and the audio editor use a new engine based on Signalsmith Stretch. Drum hits stay in time (they could drift 20 to 200 ms before); Channel settings has a choice of General, Drums / transients or Vocal / mono.

**Faster in big projects**: no UI stalls with the Mixer maximized, Playlist scrolling is 3 to 4x smoother, Missing files › Apply takes under a second instead of 25 s, and autosave does not freeze the window.
**FL effects**: Emphasizer, Frequency Shifter and Low Lifter are rebuilt and match FL Studio sample for sample. 37 FL effects are exact, 6 still approximate.

**Stand-ins for third-party plugins**: Facet EQ gets spectral dynamics per band and EQ match against a captured reference, Prism gets free band layout and 6 to 48 dB/oct slopes, and LYNX Tune's Low latency mode is about 6 ms instead of 16 ms for singing live.
fixed: **Opening the Parametric EQ froze LYNX SHARE** (since 0.1.10; it looked like a crash). Plugin editors draw without the GPU by default.
**MP3s sounded bad**: the old decoder damaged frames in more than half of the test files. MP3s also start with FL Studio's timing, so .flp projects line up again.
**Singing through FL projects**: the audio input of FL's mixer inserts is imported, so the insert you record into (with its Auto-Tune chain) plays your microphone as soon as the project opens.

**Exports no longer start with half-loaded plugins** (reported with VSTs over yabridge on Linux): before rendering, third-party plugins process about a second of silence until they have settled (Export option Plugin warm-up, on by default).
**Distortion on loud mixes**: LYNX SHARE used to bend every peak above -0.9 dBFS on the Master. Audio is untouched up to 0 dBFS, as in FL Studio, and 32-bit float WAV exports keep peaks above 0 dBFS.
**16/24-bit exports**: a third of the samples of loud passages were written one step too low.
known: EQ match cannot use a live side-chain as its reference yet.
Fruity Emphasis is still approximate.

title: Faster editing in big projects, channel arpeggiator, mixer docks
summary: Edits in projects with a lot of audio take milliseconds instead of seconds. The release also adds more of FL Studio's channel and mixer features and closer stand-ins for third-party plugins.
new: **Channel window › Misc tab**: time gate / shift, full portamento, echo delay with ping-pong and Fat mode, velocity and key tracking, and a full arpeggiator with chords from your FL Studio installation. It is imported from .flp, and live notes go through it too.
**Mixer separators, groups and docks**: tracks can be docked left, middle or right; the left and right docks stay fixed while the middle scrolls. Imported from .flp.
**Playlist track modes**: Audio and Instrument track modes, and Consolidate track, which follows tempo changes.
**Wrapper settings page** in plugin windows, with FL Studio's Settings / Processing / Troubleshooting tabs, a MIDI output port and manual latency compensation.

**Ridge Strip: Vocal strip voice**: a measured stand-in for SSL Native Vocalstrip 2 (compander, EQ, de-esser and de-ploser) that reads saved Vocalstrip states. Slate, SSL, LiquidSonics, sonible and Harrison plugins open as the closest LYNX SHARE effect when they are missing.
better: **Parameter menu** in FL Studio's sections: Init song with this position, Edit events in piano roll, Override global link, and Copy and paste value.
**Automation recording**: a control you move while recording overrides its playing automation right away.
**Import MIDI file window**: choose tracks, MIDI channels and controllers, and Blend when importing into the Piano roll.

**Prism and Echoform**: Prism gets a rebuilt Dynamic phase, Linear and Minimum phase, oversampling and an Expert panel (older projects keep their sound). Echoform gets a rhythm editor with draggable taps and 31 measured echo voicings.
The Linux AppImage can update itself with AppImageUpdate.
fixed: **Editing big projects froze LYNX SHARE**: in projects with a lot of audio (for example FL Studio's Thief demo), every edit took about 3.5 s, such as muting a channel or moving a knob. It takes a few milliseconds.
known: Notes cannot be drawn directly on Playlist instrument tracks yet.
Prism has no 6 dB/oct slopes or free bands with gaps yet.

title: Patcher, FL Studio's engines in any project, automation recording
summary: A user-editable Patcher, FL Studio's instruments and effects available in new projects, automation recording and more of FL's menus. Most of the FL engines need FL Studio installed.
new: **Patcher**: a user-editable Patcher for the Mixer (Add › Patcher) and the Channel rack (+ › Patcher). Put effects, instruments and VST3/CLAP plugins in it and connect audio, notes and control values; Patchers in .flp projects open as the same graph instead of being flattened. (#3)

**FL Studio's engines in any project**: 13 effects are in the Mixer's Add menu and 26 instruments under Channel rack › + › FL engines (Sytrus, Harmor, GMS, Ogun, FL Keys, Slayer and more). A new instance starts from the Default preset of your own FL Studio installation, so most of them need FL Studio installed. (#5)
**Newtone and Newtime editors**: in Newtone, load a sample and drag its notes; in Newtime, stretch audio with warp markers. The result can be previewed and saved as WAV.
**Automation recording**: while recording, knob moves go into automation clips (Song mode) or pattern events, with a record filter and a quantize option.
**Last tweaked**: Tools › Last tweaked parameters, and Add › Automation for last tweaked parameter.
**File › Import › MIDI file...** with FL-style options: new project or add, one channel per track or per MIDI channel, realign, mixer tracks.
**Channel window** with Plugin / Envelope / Misc tabs (cut groups, portamento, arpeggiator, polyphony).
**Voice Shift**: a new voice effect (pitch, formant, robot) that can follow MIDI notes.
better: **Menus in FL Studio's order**, with new Add and Tools menus. File › Export is per format (Wave, MP3, OGG, FLAC, MIDI), and Last exported format(s) (Ctrl+R) renders several formats at once.
**Echoform**: a Rhythm mode with draggable taps, Era modes, measured ducking and a LoFi switch.
**LYNX Tune** was re-measured against Auto-Tune Pro (retune, humanize, flex-tune, throat, natural vibrato, Classic).
fixed: Projects saved with recent Auto-Tune versions opened some scales as Chromatic instead of Minor.
First start: the welcome wizard no longer overlaps itself, and the main window fits small screens.
Imported .flp projects: Patchers that went silent are fixed, and effect names in old capitalization (Fruity delay 2) are no longer dropped.
known: Patcher: no MIDI between nodes yet, and publishing new Patcher parameters from LYNX SHARE's editor is not possible yet.
Some FL engines are not offered yet (DrumSynth Live, Wasp, Fruity Dance, Autogun, DirectWave).

title: MIDI CC automation, Formula Controller, MIDI Out, Waves crash fix
summary: Fixes and features from issues #3 and #4, a Waves crash fix on Windows and an AppImage that runs on older Linux distributions.
new: **MIDI CC automation of plugins**: every plugin's parameter menu has Automate MIDI controller: CC 0 to 127, channel aftertouch and pitch bend. This helps plugins that respond to CC64/CC1/CC11 but expose few parameters. (#3)
**Formula Controller**: a mixer effect with knobs a/b/c and a formula, using FL Studio's operators and functions. It imports from .flp. (#3)
**Envelope Controller** can be created and edited (Channel rack › + › Envelope Controller), with 8 envelopes with key ranges. (#3)
**MIDI Out**: a Channel rack generator that sends notes, CC, bank and program to the plugins on its MIDI port. Each plugin has a MIDI input port, imported from FL Studio projects. (#3)

**Recordings like FL Studio**: a saved project records into `<project folder>/Audio/Recorded` with FL-style names. When you leave a project, LYNX SHARE asks whether to delete the recordings it does not use.

**Plugin processing options**: Allow threaded processing per plugin and per mixer insert, and Process maximum size buffers as a separate option. Use fixed size buffers uses 2 ms blocks as in FL Studio.

**Small requests from #4**: View › Audio editor and View › Tempo tapper, a volume knob for Browser previews, a metronome volume control (right-click the metronome) and a Gain knob for sample channels.
better: **Export**: a new HQ for all plugins option, and the export window shows the length, total time and disk space.
**Browser search** uses an index saved between sessions, so it is faster in big folders.
fixed: **Windows: Waves plugin windows crashed LYNX SHARE** when `LYNX.exe` was in a folder with accents or other non-ASCII characters (for example a Desktop called Área de Trabalho).
**Linux: the AppImage needed glibc 2.38.** It is built on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35), so it runs on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Mint 21 and newer.
The Audio Editor, the plugin picker and the quick-add palette went behind the main window. Plugin windows keep their focus, so their drop-down menus open again. (#4)
**MIDI controllers**: enabled MIDI inputs open at startup and reconnect when a device comes back. A MIDI light in the toolbar blinks on incoming MIDI. (#4)

**Pattern length and Song mode loop**: with an empty Playlist, a 2-bar pattern loops after 2 bars instead of 1, and in Song mode the transport loops back to the start at the end of the song, as in FL Studio. (#4)
known: Patcher with audio/MIDI I/O (#3) is not done yet.
Plugins running in the separate (sandboxed) process still keep their windows above other apps.

title: Soundgoodizer fix for imported FL Studio projects
summary: A fix for Soundgoodizer in imported .flp projects on computers without FL Studio, where LYNX SHARE uses a close approximation.
better: The import report has a separate section for effects kept but approximated or partly reproduced, so only effects that were really removed appear under left out.
fixed: **Soundgoodizer slot**: on a computer without FL Studio the mixer slot showed Patcher instead of Soundgoodizer, and double-clicking it did nothing. The slot is named Soundgoodizer and opens its page (Preset A to D and Amount).
The import report listed Soundgoodizer as left out although it was still playing.

title: Linux plugin fixes: VST2, yabridge, lib64 folders, LV2
summary: Plugin fixes for Linux, reported in issue #2. After updating, open Options › Plugin manager and press Find new plugins.
new: **VST2 on Linux**: `.so` plugins in `~/.vst`, `/usr/lib/vst` and `/usr/local/lib/vst` are scanned and hosted, including yabridge bridges (`~/.vst/yabridge`). Before, LYNX SHARE hosted VST2 only on Windows.
better: **Fedora, openSUSE and other lib64 distributions**: `/usr/lib64` and `/usr/local/lib64` plugin folders (vst3, clap, lv2, vst) are part of the standard plugin folders.

**Plugin manager**: when the list is empty it says so and explains that LYNX SHARE's own instruments and effects are not listed there. They are in the Channel rack's + button, a mixer insert slot and the Quick-add palette (F8).
fixed: **LV2**: plugins in any scan folder are found and load in later sessions, not only those in the two default folders.
The scan no longer fills the terminal with `lilv_world_load_bundle(): error` lines.

title: New plugin looks, undo, A/B and presets in every engine
summary: Every built-in plugin has a new look in one of four styles, and every LYNX SHARE engine has undo / redo, A/B compare and presets. The stand-ins for missing vocal plugins were measured against the originals and sound closer.
new: **Four plugin styles**: Glow, Neon, Hardware and Vivid. Each plugin has its own style by default; Settings › General › Plugin style can force one everywhere, and there is a Reduced effects option for weak graphics cards.
**Undo, A/B and presets in every LYNX SHARE engine**: undo / redo of its own edits, A/B with copy, and a preset menu with factory presets plus your own.
better: **More controls in the engines**: Facet EQ (per-band on/off and L / R / M / S placement, auto gain), Apex Limiter (8 styles, dither), Crest Compressor, Sentry Gate, Hush De-esser, Ember and Prism gained controls their classics have.
**LYNX Tune**: Flex-Tune, Natural Vibrato, Hold, Auto Key, per-note bypass / remove and more scales, in an editor laid out like Auto-Tune's Auto mode.

**Stand-ins for missing vocal plugins**: measured on real vocal takes, Ridge Strip is within 0.05 dB of SSL E-Channel in tone, Echoform within 0.1 dB of H-Delay in level, and Glow within about 0.4 dB of CLA-2A. Old projects keep their previous sound: the new voicings only apply to stand-in slots.
known: The Renaissance Compressor stand-in is closer but still 1.5 to 4 dB off, and is still being refined.

title: Faster Waves projects, Quell Denoiser, Gemini Doubler
summary: Vocal projects that use Waves plugins open faster, without freezing, and with the right plugin in every slot. There are two new effects, and LYNX Tune follows Waves Tune settings more closely.
new: **Quell Denoiser**: six-band noise reduction with one Amount fader, in NS1's role. Saved NS1 settings carry over.
**Gemini Doubler**: two pitch-shifted delay voices with a direct-signal row, in Doubler's role. Two-voice Doubler settings carry over.
better: **Opening projects with Waves plugins**: the Waves shell starts in the background and stays loaded, so the window no longer freezes while Waves' service starts (longest freeze 13 s down to about 1.5 s). After 8 s the progress panel offers Continue without it, and those slots get LYNX SHARE substitutes.
**H-Delay settings carry over to Echoform**: tempo sync / ms, note, feedback, ping-pong, mix, output and filters. Echoform gains Output and Pairs controls.
**LYNX Tune** reads Waves Tune's key and scale (custom scales too) and its Note Transition time, and each phrase starts from the sung pitch.

**Performance against FL Studio 2026 on the same PC**: demo projects opened in 3.6 to 9.4 s (FL: 6.0 to 10.2 s) and used 126 to 391 MB of RAM after opening (FL: 806 to 930 MB). Playback CPU matches FL's.
fixed: The first Waves plugin of a project could load as a different Waves plugin, because the Waves shell reorders its list when it starts. LYNX SHARE checks the name; if it still cannot create the right one, the slot shows a load failure instead of playing the wrong plugin.

title: macOS and Linux builds, project backups, crash-proof plugin hosting
summary: The first release for Windows, macOS and Linux. It adds FL-style backups and project packages, plugin hosting that survives a plugin crash, and a progress panel while projects open.
new: **macOS and Linux builds**: native builds of the whole app, for macOS 11+ (Intel and Apple silicon) and Linux x86_64 (AppImage or .tar.gz).

**Backups and versions**: backups named like FL's (Song (autosaved on ... at ...)), and the file a save replaces is kept as an overwritten backup. File › Save new version (Ctrl+Alt+S) and File › Revert to last backup... are new, and after a bad exit the next start offers the newest backup.

**Project packages**: File › Collect project samples into a folder... and Export project with samples (.zip); opening a .zip unpacks and opens it. Moved projects find their samples next to the project file.
**Per-plugin Processing submenu** (channel and mixer slot menus): Use fixed size buffers (latency compensated) and Run in a separate process.
**Browser tabs**: Current project (the project's audio files) and Starred (right-click › Starred).
**Toolbar edit mode**: remove, move and change toolbar items.
better: **A hosted plugin that crashes no longer takes LYNX SHARE down**: instruments go silent, effects pass their input through, and the slot is marked.

**Opening projects**: a progress panel shows what is loading (samples, plugins, mixer), and samples are read, decoded and stretched on background threads. A big vocal project no longer shows Not responding while it opens.

**Waves vocal chains**: Renaissance Compressor, DeEsser, CLA-2A and SSL E-Channel states are read and their settings translated to LYNX SHARE's Compressor, Hush De-esser, Glow Leveler and Ridge Strip. Auto-Tune Pro's key and scale go to LYNX Tune.
Mixer worker threads park when the transport is stopped, which lowers idle CPU. The CPU meter has an underrun counter.
fixed: Waves shells get a longer scan and a retry, and a plugin installed in a new folder is found instead of the stale old entry.
Two edge cases in built-in effects: Delay Bank at 192 kHz and Maximus with NaN input.
known: The macOS build is not notarized yet: right-click › Open the first time.

title: Ten native reverbs, delays and modulators, Playlist track groups
summary: Ten new reverbs, delays and modulators in LYNX SHARE's own code, exact Fruity Phaser and Fruity Send engines, a rewritten Facet EQ editor and FL-style Playlist and Channel rack groups. It also contains the level fixes behind vocals that were quieter than in FL Studio.
new: **Six reverbs** on one engine: Epoch Verb (22 modes), Atrium (rooms), Foil Plate, Nebula (huge spaces), Halo (shimmer) and Horizon. Projects that used Valhalla reverbs you do not have open with these, with every saved value translated.
**Delays and modulation**: Echoform (multi-style delay), Spiral Echo (frequency-shifting echo), Orbit (space modulator) and Lattice Mod (chorus / flanger / ensemble).

**Dynamics**: Crest Compressor (side chain, auto gain), Prism Multiband (four-band dynamics) and Sentry Gate. Projects that used the classic plugins in those roles open with the saved settings translated.
**Fruity Phaser and Fruity Send on exact engines**: Phaser is bit-identical to FL's on all 27 presets; Send has FL's routing (level / pan matrix, dry, plugin delay compensation).
**Playlist track groups and Channel rack filter groups**: track groups fold and unfold, with FL's track and channel menus. The Mixer side panel follows FL's layout.
**LYNX ASIO input**: exclusive and shared capture through LYNX SHARE's ASIO driver, and a 32-bit driver DLL packaged alongside the 64-bit one.
better: **Facet EQ editor** rewritten: full-window graph with analyser, draggable nodes, dynamic EQ bands, natural / linear phase modes and band solo. LYNX Tune shows the detected and corrected pitch live.
**FL-arranged windows** for Fruity Vocoder, Frequency Splitter, Delay Bank, EQUO, Multiband Delay, Convolver, Pitch Shifter, Effector, Hardcore and Vocodex.
**Mixer**: editable route-to-Master level knob.
fixed: **Vocals quieter than in FL Studio**: mixer route levels (insert to insert and to Master) follow FL's fader curve, overlapping audio clips of one channel both play, and compressor substitutes apply auto gain. Verified within 0.1 to 0.5 dB of FL Studio on a real vocal project.
Audio clips keep the sub-tick part of millisecond offsets and start on a whole source frame like FL Studio.

title: FL Studio 26 projects, microphone input, LYNX ASIO, native plugins
summary: FL Studio 26 projects play complete and at the right level, and the crackles on heavy projects are gone at the default buffer. The release adds microphone input on every mixer insert, LYNX SHARE's own ASIO driver, eleven native plugins and an audio editor.
new: **Microphone / input**: every mixer insert has an input selector (stereo pairs or single channels), record arm, monitoring mode and a live input meter. The record button asks what to record: audio into the Playlist, into the audio editor, notes, or everything.
**LYNX ASIO**: LYNX SHARE's own ASIO driver, in shared mode (other apps keep their sound) or exclusive for the lowest latency. Register LYNX ASIO.bat makes it available to other programs.
**LYNX Tune**: real-time vocal pitch correction with key/scale, retune speed, humanize, formant preserve, MIDI target notes and a low-latency mode.
**Facet EQ and Apex Limiter**: an 8-band EQ and a true-peak limiter.
**Mixing suite**: Ridge Strip (channel strip), Glow Leveler (optical leveler), Hush De-esser, Aether (air) and Ember Saturator (tube / tape / transistor / fuzz).

**Missing plugins get a LYNX SHARE equivalent**: when a project uses a plugin you do not have, LYNX SHARE opens its native equivalent and keeps the original's settings untouched, so the original comes back once it is installed. It can be turned off in Settings › General.
**Audio editor**: waveform / spectrogram, selections, markers, edits, recording, save, and send to Playlist or Sampler.

**New windows**: Export (WAV / MP3 / OGG / FLAC, stems, dither, normalize), New project with templates, Clip properties, Plugin manager, Shortcut manager, Event editor and the Piano roll tools (quantize, chop, flam, LFO, riff machine, chord progression).
better: **Plugin windows laid out like their FL counterparts**: Limiter, Parametric EQ 2, Delay 3, Multiband Compressor, Soundgoodizer, Reeverb 2, Maximus, Gross Beat, FL Keys, 3x Osc and more, drawn in LYNX SHARE's own style.
**Settings › Audio** explains each driver: Windows Audio shared, low-latency shared, exclusive (down to about 3 ms on capable devices) and DirectSound.
**Zoom tool** in the Playlist and Piano roll: click zooms in, drag zooms to a range, right-click zooms out.
Newtone renders pitch edits, and FL's VST2 plugins load with their saved state.
fixed: **Projects saved by FL Studio 25.2+ / 26 were missing most clips** and sounded much quieter. LYNX SHARE reads the new playlist record, clip gain and fades; on a real user project it is within 0.5 dB of FL's own render.

**More FL level fixes**: mixer routes to inserts 100+ with no saved level played silent, audio clips were 5.2 dB too quiet, and Maximus in linear-phase mode and old wrapped Fruity Compressors lost their settings.

**Crackles**: Patchers no longer rebuild during playback, linear-phase FFTs are faster and worker threads use Windows' Pro Audio scheduling. The heaviest demos have no late blocks at the new default 512-sample buffer.
**Clip menu**: it opens from the clip's icon, and right-click on the header deletes the clip, as in FL Studio.

title: Stuck-note fix, FL-style Playlist clips, Missing files window
summary: Preview notes always stop, Playlist clips are drawn the FL way with a full clip menu, and there are new Missing files and Settings windows. Imported FL Studio projects sound closer thanks to FL's sampler voice and exact Ogg Vorbis decoding.
new: **Clip menu** (right-click a clip or its icon): Rename and color, Make unique, Split here, Chop to grid, Merge clips, Reverse, Normalize, Clip volume, Fit to tempo, Open in a new Sampler channel, Mute and more. Every action is one undo step.

**Missing files window** (Help › Missing files..., also shown after opening a project with missing samples): lists the missing samples and plugins, searches the remembered, Browser and project folders by itself, and applies the found files as one undo step.

**Settings window** (Options › Project settings... / Project info... / File settings...): tempo, time signature, swing and master pitch; project info (imported from FL projects); search, Browser and plugin folders.
better: **Playlist clips, FL style**: a slim header with a kind icon and the name, audio drawn as one filled waveform and pattern clips as thin note bars. The spectral colouring is still an option (Options › Waveforms).
**A lighter header**: finer icon strokes, smaller toolbar rows, a slim flat transport, and a tip with the tool's name and shortcut when you rest the mouse on a button.
**Native sampler voice**: imported sampler channels run FL's whole voice: velocity and pan laws, the channel filter (all 8 types), the envelopes and LFOs, WAV loop points and the end fade.
**Harmor**: image synthesis, arpeggio envelopes, noise resonance, pluck blend, and phaser and harmonizer masks.
**FL Slayer**: the channel's volume, pan and pitch act as FL sends them, and parameter automation reaches the running engine.
fixed: **Stuck notes**: every press-to-preview path stops its note when you let go: Channel rack steps, the Piano roll keyboard, note clicks, the typing keyboard and MIDI keyboards.
**Ogg Vorbis samples**: many FL factory samples are Ogg streams inside `.wav` files. The previous decoder dropped blocks in 295 of them; they are decoded as FL Studio does.

title: Installer, setup wizard, background plugin scanning, spectral waveforms
summary: A per-user installer with a first-run setup wizard, plugin scanning in the background and a customizable toolbar. Another batch of FL Studio generators and effects runs on engines rebuilt from FL's own.
new: **Installer**: per user, no admin rights. It adds a Start-menu shortcut, opens `.lynx` files, offers Open with for .flp (FL Studio stays the default program) and uninstalls from Apps & features; the portable zip is still there.
**Setup wizard** on the first start (later: Options › Setup wizard): language, audio device, plugin folders (the standard VST3/CLAP folders and FL Studio's), scan.

**Plugin scanning in the background**: incremental and cancellable, with progress in the hint bar. Each file is scanned in its own child process, so a crashing or hanging plugin is blacklisted instead of taking LYNX SHARE down.
**Customizable toolbar**: show, hide and reorder groups, small or large icons, UI scale.
**Spectral waveforms**: audio clips, the Sampler and the Browser draw band-coloured waveforms.
**FL generators on their exact engines**: SimSynth, BeepMap, Sawer, Fruity Granulizer, Drumaxx, DirectWave, FL Slayer and FL Keys. Wasp / Wasp XT load as a silent placeholder (their state is kept).
better: **FL Studio projects**: plugins resolve from LYNX SHARE's list or FL Studio's own plugin database, and samples are relocated from FL's folders, other PC/user paths and the project folder.
**Sample players**: Sampler channels and audio clips read samples through FL's own interpolators, with FL's volume envelope for sampler channels.

**FL effects on their exact engines**: Fruity Love Philter, Fruity Vocoder, Hardcore, Distructor, Multiband Delay, Flangus, Flanger, Delay Bank, Multiband Compressor, LuxeVerb, Convolver, EQUO, Pitch Shifter and several filters. Newtone and Newtime are imported with their state (pass-through).
**Browser** rework (tree, preview strip, fold keys) and editor additions: Line/Events snap, drum brush, stretch handle, editable ghost notes, track heights.
**Faster export**: WaveShaper, Fruity Limiter, Reeverb 2 and MiniSynth use less CPU with the same output.

title: FL-style interface, Brazilian Portuguese, more FL Studio plugin engines
summary: A new FL-style interface, a Brazilian Portuguese translation, and a large batch of FL Studio generators and effects rebuilt from their own engines.
new: **FL-style layout**: new main toolbar, shared editor title bars, window menus, and a workspace with the Channel rack as a pop-up and floating panels over the Playlist.
**Hint bar** with mouse/key glyphs and live values while you drag a knob or fader.
**Português (Brasil)**: switch in Options › Language (or `--lang pt-BR`). English stays the default.
**Recording options**: count-in, wait for input, overdub/replace, record quantise and per-insert arm.
